newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran denies backing PUK in Iraqi Kurdish fighting.
newsitem.headline: Iran denies backing PUK in Iraqi Kurdish fighting.

text.p: Iran denied on Monday its troops were backing the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) forces battling a rival pro-Baghdad group for supremacy in northern Iraq.

Foreign ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi, quoted by Tehran radio, denied the charges by Massoud Barzani, leader of the Baghdad-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) that Iranian troops were helping PUK forces sweeping across the region.

Mohammadi said the charges were raised as a reaction to "protests by international bodies because of the collaboration of Barzani with the Iraqi army in suppressing the defenceless Kurdish people and turning them into refugees".
Barzani on Sunday accused Iranian forces of helping the PUK retake the key city of Sulaimaniya and called for international aid against "Iran's brutal invasion".
U.N. officials and guards in Iraqi Kurdistan said on Monday that PUK forces had regained control of most of the territory they lost to the KDP six weeks ago.
Iran has repeatedly denied backing the PUK.
State-run Tehran radio called on the KDP and PUK to cease fighting and seek a negotiated solution to the conflict.
"Fighting will lead to nothing other than disappointment and unhappiness for the people of this war-torn region," it said.
Inter-Kurdish fighting was also allowing Iraq and the United States to meddle in the area, the radio said in a commentary.
Baghdad has said its intrusion in Kurdish northern Iraq in late August, which helped the KDP capture the Kurdish capital Arbil, was aimed at backing the KDP against the PUK and Iran.
Tehran has said its occasional intrusions into northern Iraq, such as an attack in July, targeted Iranian Kurdish rebels based there.
A local Iranian official said on Monday some of the 65,000 refugees Kurdish refugees who fled to Iran following the KDP sweep were preparing to return home after the PUK advances.
Marivan city governor Ali Yari said about 1,000 refugees had already left and more were expected to follow, the Iranian news agency IRNA reported.
